cases.title: WordCount job had failing map tasks

groundTruth.cause: The local disk on one cluster node filled up, so map tasks running there could not write their output (no valid local directory) and had to be killed and re-run on other nodes.
keyEvidence: Could not find any valid local directory
goodNextSteps: Check free disk space on the node's YARN local directories (df on yarn.nodemanager.local-dirs)
Check which node the failed attempts ran on and whether YARN marked its disks unhealthy

answer.summary: The WordCount MapReduce job experienced map task failures and prolonged execution due to excessive map output sizes exceeding the configured maxSingleShuffleLimit, leading to on-disk shuffling and significant I/O overhead. This caused delays in the reduce phase and overall job duration.

cases.title: WordCount map tasks killed after retries

groundTruth.cause: One cluster node was disconnected from the network, so tasks could not reach HDFS datanodes on it (NoRouteToHost) to read their input blocks and were killed after retries.
goodNextSteps: Check network connectivity to the datanode address in the errors (ping, routes, switch port, firewall)
Check the HDFS datanode report for dead or unreachable nodes

app.reason: No error-level findings, so the app refuses to investigate (the API returns 400).

answer.summary: The provided log snippet shows a MapReduce job where map tasks are progressing through spilling and merging map outputs, and ultimately completing successfully. There is no evidence of map tasks being killed or failing after retries. The log ends with a successful completion message indicating the task is done and committing. Therefore, there is no actual incident of map tasks being killed after retries as described in the incident title.

goodNextSteps: Check network connectivity from the application master's node to the ResourceManager and NameNode
